heard: The first photograph of Earth from space was taken by a weapon. On October 24, 1946, researchers launched a captured German V-2 rocket from White Sands, New Mexico. Clyde Holiday of the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory secured a modified 35-millimeter camera inside. V-2 Number 13 soared roughly 65 miles high, crossing the 100-kilometer edge of space. That reached five times the altitude of a 1935 balloon record. The lens captured Earth's curved horizon, set against the blackness of space. Plunging back down, the rocket slammed into the desert at high speed, obliterating its airframe. Yet the exposed film negative survived intact inside a protective steel cassette.
